newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany wants signal of hope for NATO rejects.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants signal of hope for NATO rejects.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Thursday it was vital that NATO remained open to further new members after next month's Madrid summit to decide on the alliance's eastward expansion.

Kinkel said Germany could live with a decision in Madrid to extend invitations to three new members, as favoured by the United States, or to a larger number. Sources in Bonn have indicated privately Germany supports the U.S. position.
"What is decisive at the same time is the signal to those states which are not part of the first group," Kinkel told a parliamentary debate on NATO. "The alliance remains open."
Kinkel said Germany and Britain had put forward a joint suggestion for a clear passage on this point for inclusion in a declaration to be issued at the summit.
"Above all the Baltic states expect a signal from Madrid," Kinkel said. "They do not want to be pushed to the margins when the alliance opens up."
The Baltic states are widely expected to be excluded from the first wave of new NATO members.
Washington wants only Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to be invited to join at Madrid. France and some other alliance states would prefer membership for Romania and Slovenia at the same time.
